Hands-on guide ① · No LiteLLM (Direct SDK)

Make Claude Code answer
with GitHub Copilot models

No gateway in the middle — one local bridge is all you need. Install → sign in → check → run. Follow those four steps and a Copilot model answers OK right in your Claude Code window.

  • About 10 min total
  • macOS · Linux
  • No Anthropic API key needed
  • Prompts count toward your Copilot usage
Follow along from the start → Watch the video first

The SDK has been renamed: GitHub Copilot SDK (@github/copilot-sdk) → Microsoft Copilot SDK (@microsoft/copilot-sdk). This guide is based on version 2.0.0.

Before you start

Have these six things ready and you can start right away.

  • macOS or LinuxThe default Windows shell is not supported.
  • Claude CodeYou need the claude command.
  • GitHub Copilot CLIThe copilot command. If you don't have it, you'll install it in step 2.
  • Node.js ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0Check with node -v.
  • curl and Git
  • GitHub Copilot accessYou can only use models that your organization's Copilot policy allows.
This is an unofficial integration

Neither Anthropic nor GitHub (Microsoft) officially supports this combination. Every prompt you send counts against your own GitHub Copilot usage (AI Credits). It's best suited to personal experiments and research.

1

Install

Download the repository and install its dependencies.

About 1 min
  1. In your home directory, clone the repository, move into it, and install the dependencies.
Terminal
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/junwoojeong100/cc-mscp-sdk-v2.git cc-mscp-sdk
cd cc-mscp-sdk
npm ci
What success looks like
  • npm ci finishes without errors and you see added … packages in …s.
  • A cc-mscp-sdk folder now exists.
What if I see a vulnerabilities warning at the end?

npm can print an N vulnerabilities warning at the end of an install. Whether it appears depends on the npm registry you use and when you install, and it did not appear in the screenshot above. When this repository was checked in advance (2026-11-24), the warnings came from development and test dependencies, and npm audit --omit=dev, which checks only the dependencies used at runtime, reported 0 findings. Even if you see the warning, this guide does not run npm audit fix and simply continues.

Folder name

The repository is named cc-mscp-sdk-v2, but to keep the commands and screens that follow short, this guide adds the folder name cc-mscp-sdk to the end of git clone. If you cloned into a different folder, substitute its name in the commands that follow.

npm ci fails
  • Check that node -v prints a version that satisfies ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0.
  • If you use a company registry or a proxy, check that npm config get registry is an address you can reach.
  • Make sure you ran it inside the cc-mscp-sdk folder (the one that contains package-lock.json).
Next: Copilot sign-in →
2

Sign in to GitHub Copilot

Sign in with the Copilot CLI. You don't need an Anthropic API key.

About 2 min
  1. Check that the copilot command exists. If it prints a path, it's installed.
  2. If nothing is printed, install the Copilot CLI.
  3. Sign in. On your own computer (a desktop), a browser opens automatically. Approve the request on the GitHub authorization page. If it doesn't open, copy the address shown on screen and paste it into your browser.
Terminal
command -v copilot
Install (only if missing)
npm install -g @github/copilot
Terminal
copilot login
Working over SSH or in a container?

On a remote environment, the one-time code flow is used automatically. Open the address on screen in a browser and enter the code. To use this flow on your own computer too, run copilot login --device-code.

What success looks like
  • command -v copilot prints a path.
  • After you approve in the browser, the terminal finishes signing you in and returns to the prompt. The token is kept in your system credential store (or, if there isn't one, in a config file under ~/.copilot/).
  • If ghcp-models in the next step shows a list, you're signed in.
Already signed in?

If this computer is already signed in to the Copilot CLI, you can skip this step. Confirm by checking that step 3 shows a model list.

Next: Check environment and models →
3

Check the environment and models

Make sure the tools are installed correctly and see which models your account can use.

About 1 min
  1. From the repository folder (~/cc-mscp-sdk), check your environment.
  2. Then look at the list of models your account can use.
~/cc-mscp-sdk
./bin/ghcp-doctor
~/cc-mscp-sdk
./bin/ghcp-models
What success looks like
  • All four items in the ghcp-doctor output show "ok": true.
  • ghcp-models prints several model lines (for example, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4.5).
A model list is not a response check

ghcp-models only shows the models your account can access; it does not check whether a model actually answers. You'll confirm a real response in step 4.

It fails or shows an odd message
  • claude: false or Claude Code executable not found… — Install Claude Code, or set CLAUDE_CODE_BIN to the path of the real executable (it must not be this repository's launcher).
  • SDK protocol version mismatch — The Copilot CLI that COPILOT_CLI_PATH points to is out of date. Run unset COPILOT_CLI_PATH and try again. (Inside a Copilot CLI session, this variable is set.)
  • Authentication error — Run copilot login from step 2 again. Signing in again doesn't fix every error.
Next: Run Claude Code →
4

Run Claude Code

Run the launcher from the project folder you want to work in, then send your first question.

About 1 min
  1. Go to the project folder you want to work in. (Not the repository folder.)
  2. Run the repository's launcher by its absolute path. You don't need to change your PATH.
  3. If this is the first time you've opened the folder, a trust prompt appears. The default choice is No, exit, so press ↓ to select Yes, I trust this folder, then press Enter.
  4. Type Reply with OK in the input box and press Enter.
Terminal
cd ~/my-project
~/cc-mscp-sdk/bin/claude-ghcp
What success looks like
  • The header shows a GitHub Copilot · … model name.
  • When you send your question in the input box, the answer OK comes back.
  • To quit, type /exit. You're back at your shell.
What does this prove?

If an answer comes back, one request has gone through Claude Code → bridge → SDK → Copilot and completed. That doesn't mean every feature has been verified. The starting model is chosen in this order: --ghcp-model → the exported GHCP_MODEL → claude-sonnet-5.

It won't start, or the request fails
  • Dependencies are missing… — Run npm ci in the repository folder (step 1).
  • GitHub Copilot model is unavailable: … — Pass --ghcp-model with a model that appears in ./bin/ghcp-models.
  • Persistent bridge exited; inspect …/bridge.log — Read the last lines of the log it points to. The cause is written there.
  • A turn looks stuck for more than a minute — Copilot may have hit a rate limit and be waiting while it retries on its own.
Next: Switch models →
5

Switch models

Change the model mid-conversation, or pick one when you start.

About 2 min

Option ASwitch during a conversation

  1. Type /model in the Claude Code input box.
  2. Use ↑ ↓ to pick a model. Rows labeled GitHub Copilot · … are the models this bridge provides. The screenshot below picks GPT-6 Sol.
  3. Press s. It applies to this session only.
  4. If the conversation is already under way, a Switch model? confirmation appears. Press Enter to choose 1. Yes, switch to ….
  5. Send the same question again (Reply with OK). The new model answers.
Prefer s over Enter

Below the list you'll see s to use this session only · Enter to save. Enter saves the model you picked as the default for the next session. It actually changes the model entry in ~/.claude/settings.json, so it can also affect Claude Code when you use it with its original provider. In this guide, use s (this session only).

Option BPick the model at launch

Terminal
cd ~/my-project
~/cc-mscp-sdk/bin/claude-ghcp --ghcp-model claude-haiku-4.5

Option CAsk once and exit (print mode)

Terminal
cd ~/my-project
~/cc-mscp-sdk/bin/claude-ghcp --ghcp-model claude-haiku-4.5 -p "Reply with OK only"
What success looks like
  • The /model list shows GitHub Copilot · … rows.
  • Your question still gets an answer after the switch.
Good to know
  • claude-ghcp does not accept --model. Choose the model with --ghcp-model.
  • Models that aren't in the list can also be used with --ghcp-model if your policy allows them, but that hasn't been verified.
Next: Check status and stop →
6

Check the bridge status and stop it

The bridge keeps running even after you quit Claude Code. Check its status, and stop it when you need to.

About 1 min
  1. You can check the status from any folder. It shows the pid, the port, the model the bridge started with, and the number of replaced bridges (retired).
  2. (Optional) Check the log to see which model answered.
  3. When you're done with it, stop the bridge.
Terminal
~/cc-mscp-sdk/bin/claude-ghcp-status

OptionalCheck the log to see which model answered

For every completed turn, the bridge writes one line to bridge.log with the requested model and the model the SDK reported (it doesn't include conversation content). Count the turns per model.

Terminal
grep -o '"requestedModel":"[^"]*","model":"[^"]*"' ~/Library/Caches/claude-code-ghcp-sdk/bridge.log | sort | uniq -c

On Linux, the log is at ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/claude-code-ghcp-sdk/bridge.log. This check is based on the model ID the SDK reported; it doesn't independently prove the provider's internal implementation.

Terminal
~/cc-mscp-sdk/bin/claude-ghcp-stop
Before you stop it

claude-ghcp-stop disconnects every session and /background job that uses the shared bridge. Finish any work in progress and copy any logs you need before you run it. It doesn't delete your user settings or saved conversations.

Next: PATH setup (optional) →
7

Optional: launch with the claude command

Put the repository's bin at the front of your PATH, and typing just claude starts the Direct launcher.

About 1 min

This isn't an extra install step. If it feels like a hassle, skip it and keep using the absolute-path method from step 4. These instructions are for Zsh.

Terminal
cd ~/cc-mscp-sdk
echo "export PATH=\"$PWD/bin:\$PATH\"" >> ~/.zshrc
exec zsh
command -v claude
To undo it
  • To run Claude Code with its original provider, use claude-current.
  • To remove the PATH change, delete that export line from ~/.zshrc and open a new terminal.
Next: Troubleshooting table →

Troubleshooting at a glance

These are the symptoms you're most likely to run into. For more, see the Diagnostics guide.

Symptom / messageCauseFix
SDK protocol version mismatchCOPILOT_CLI_PATH points to an outdated Copilot CLIRun unset COPILOT_CLI_PATH and try again (or point it at the latest CLI)
Claude Code executable not found…The real Claude Code executable can't be foundInstall Claude Code, or set its path in CLAUDE_CODE_BIN
Dependencies are missing…npm ci was not runRun npm ci in the repository folder
GitHub Copilot model is unavailable: …A model ID your account can't usePass --ghcp-model with an ID from ./bin/ghcp-models
Persistent bridge exited; inspect …The bridge exited right after startingCheck the last error in the bridge.log it points to
Authentication error when listing modelsCopilot sign-in expired or missingcopilot login
A turn is unresponsive for over a minuteThe runtime is waiting to retry after a Copilot rate limitWait a moment. If every retry fails, it's returned as 429/529 and Claude Code retries

About this guide

  • The screenshots and video on this page were captured from real runs in the environment below. The folders on screen (such as ~/my-project) are for recording, one-time authentication values are masked with *, and some lines of the model list are omitted.
  • This is an unofficial integration that uses GitHub Copilot models in Claude Code. Neither Anthropic nor GitHub (Microsoft) supports this combination.
  • This guide shows one request being processed from start to finish. The 36 cases of the essential suite were not re-run with SDK 2.0.0; for the scope, see What works and what does not.

Tested environment (recorded 2026-11-25): macOS · Node.js v22.16.0 · Claude Code 2.1.331 · @microsoft/copilot-sdk 2.0.0 (runtime 1.0.113)
